channels.name: JP Carpentry Ltd
channels.description: A working carpenter (fitted furniture specialist) who also sells training courses, including 'Wardrobe Pro', to help other tradespeople build the same skill into a business. UK-based, not Nigeria-specific, but a genuine, dedicated, on-topic channel.
channels.focus: Fitted furniture trade + skills training business
channels.verificationMethod: Found via broader search. Channel self-description directly confirms both the craft and the business-of-training angle. Jumoke Dada (founder of Nigerian furniture brand Taeillo, Wikipedia-notable, TechCrunch-covered) was also researched at length — extensively real and well-documented, but appears only as a guest across several different interview shows (Young CEO, Tech Turks, African Business Stories), not as the owner of her own dedicated channel, so wasn't counted as 'her channel'.

blogs.name: BusinessDay Nigeria
blogs.verificationMethod: Same feed already verified for Agriculture and Dentistry — cross-tagged here because BusinessDay has run specific, real furniture-making business features (e.g. 'The burgeoning business of furniture-making, interior decoration', profiling Lagos-based carpenter/entrepreneur Blessing Ohikhena Sule).

notes: Genuinely thorough search for a free book came up empty on the business side specifically: plenty of free woodworking/craft-technique ebooks exist (Project Gutenberg, CraftsmanSpace, WoodWorkWeb), but they teach the craft, which the target user already has — not pricing, clients, or running the business, which is what this category needs. The one book found that WAS business-focused ('Start Your Own Woodworking Business' by Norman Pirollo) is a paid $15 ebook bundled with a course. Left at 0/10 rather than count a craft book as if it were business content.
